claims.text: The target materials are high-entropy alloys initially in a solid state.
Deep-learning potentials can improve determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature in high-entropy alloys.
Deep-learning potentials can improve determination of fusion enthalpy in high-entropy alloys.
Deep-learning potentials can improve determination of fusion entropy in high-entropy alloys.
Deep-learning potentials can improve determination of volume change at the transition in high-entropy alloys.
Deep-learning potentials can improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention is applicable to high-temperature, multicomponent systems.
Local chemical clustering and short-range ordering mediate the effect of deep-learning potentials on thermodynamic-property prediction.
Deep-learning potentials enhance the representation of structural and chemical complexity in high-entropy materials.
Enhanced representation of structural and chemical complexity leads to more accurate thermodynamic-property predictions.
The proposed predictions will be more accurate than existing experimental, DFT, and CALPHAD baselines.
Applicability is limited to high-entropy alloys with complex chemical and structural properties.
Transferability of deep-learning potentials across alloy systems and properties remains uncertain.
A comparison against experimental measurements across a range of high-entropy alloys can test the predictions.
Significant deviation of predicted properties from experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
